newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin to meet target state budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin to meet target state budget deficit.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Thursday that despite lower-than-expected revenues, the country's full-year budget deficit target would not be excceeded due to recently adopted measures.
"The full year deficit should not be higher than the planned 27 billion crowns as the government has been adopting measures to compensate expected lower revenues," Kozlik told Parliament.

The budget deficit widened sharply to 13.4 billion crowns for the January-September period from 7.9 billion in the first eight months of 1996, while the full-year deficit projection is 26.95 billion crowns.
Last week the cabinet moved to stop the budget deficit figure being overshot, freezing expenditures across the board, except for the Social Affairs and Interior Ministries.
Kozlik said that according to the latest forecast, overall state budget revenues for 1996 should be lower by some two billion crowns than the planned 165.46 billion.
He added that the cabinet has been gradually reducing expenditures in all budget allocations by a total of 1.9 billion crowns.
"This amount should compensate lower revenues and ensure the overal deficit will not be higher than expected," he said.
However, Kozlik said that according to International Monetary Fund (IMF) standards, Slovakia posted fiscal surplus of 0.4 billion crowns for the January-September period.
"When we deduct the sum of 13.8 billion crowns, which went to debt sevicing we get a fiscal surplus," Kozlik added.
